title: Your Customers Stopped Calling. Are You Answering Texts?
summary: Younger customers avoid phone calls, and most service businesses respond slowly to texts and forms. Here's what that costs you and how to fix it.
context:
Angle: home service businesses still run on phone calls, but a growing share of customers would rather text or fill out a form, and most shops are slow or silent on those channels. Speed to lead decides who gets the job, and AI is the only way a small shop can respond in under a minute, 24/7, on every channel.

Key findings to verify and cite:
- Gen Z: 47% feel anxious when someone calls them (vs 32% of all adults); 87% list texting as a top-3 way to communicate vs 49% for calls; 36% don't listen to voicemail. weBoost Good Call Survey, 2020, 1,000 US adults: https://assets.wilsonelectronics.com/m/3788b144e055bd3f/original/weBoost-Good-Call-Survey-Full-Report-Presentation.pdf
- Millennials: 88% prefer texting over calling, 52% feel anxious when the phone rings. HighSpeedInternet.com, 2020, 500 US adults (small sample, note it): https://www.notebookcheck.net/Phone-calls-what-are-those-Most-US-millennials-are-found-to-be-more-comfortable-with-texting.459437.0.html
- Nearly 70% of 18-34s prefer texting to calls. Uswitch, 2,000 people, UK, 2025: https://jang.com.pk/en/54151-gen-z-millennials-phone-phobia-70-young-adults-prefer-texts-over-calls-news
- 67% prefer appointment messages by text; 58% have texted back after a missed call from a business; only 39% of businesses texted customers. Zipwhip 2019 State of Texting: https://martech.org/new-survey-consumers-are-texting-to-businesses-that-arent-set-up-to-respond-2/
- Only 52% of calls to home services businesses reached a person; 66% of buyers hung up on an unanswered call; 51% stopped after one provider. Invoca 2026, via https://stealthagents.com/research/home-services-missed-call-revenue-statistics-2026 (find the Invoca primary source if possible)
- Secret shopper test of 466 HVAC, plumbing and home improvement companies: only 60% responded to a service request within five days; no response in 6 hours meant a 75% chance of never responding. Valve+Meter via Pro Remodeler: https://www.proremodeler.com/business/financials/article/55187904/a-5-day-look-at-response-times
- Responding within 5 minutes vs 30 minutes: ~100x more likely to reach the lead, ~21x more likely to qualify; 1 hour response 7x more likely to have a meaningful conversation. Oldroyd/MIT and InsideSales, HBR 2011 'The Short Life of Online Sales Leads' (cite HBR directly).

Caveats to state honestly: some surveys are older or small samples, and several speed-to-lead stats come from vendors that sell response tools. Treat them as directional.

Solvr Labs section: how an AI agent answers missed calls, replies to texts and web forms instantly, and books the job, in the customer's preferred channel and in English or Spanish. Tie to Radar and TaskLine using only facts from the site. Practical next step for readers: test your own business by calling, texting and submitting your web form after hours, and time the responses. CTA to /assessment or /radar.
